proposed_fix.description: Confirm whether recommendationservice is leaking or piling up sockets (connections not closed, or slow downstream calls), then relieve it with a gated, reversible restart or scale-out while the root cause is investigated.
steps: Inspect socket state for the recommendationservice pods (e.g. `kubectl exec <pod> -- ss -s` and `ss -tan | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c`) to see whether sockets are ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT or CLOSE_WAIT.
Check the pods' logs and outbound connections for unclosed gRPC/HTTP clients, missing connection reuse, or slow upstream dependencies (e.g. productcatalogservice) that would hold sockets open.
Compare the socket, CPU and memory growth timeline (E1, E9) with recent deploys or config changes to the service; if a recent change correlates, prepare to roll it back.
With human approval, scale recommendationservice out by one or more replicas to spread load and reduce per-pod socket and CPU pressure.

If CLOSE_WAIT or leaked sockets are confirmed and latency is still degraded, with human approval do a rolling restart of the recommendationservice pods one at a time, watching socket and latency metrics after each.
Optionally, check node conntrack usage (R1) only if socket exhaustion is confirmed to be reaching node-level limits.
preconditions: Confirm the socket spike (E8) is still ongoing and not already recovered.
Confirm other replicas are healthy and capacity exists in the cluster before scaling or restarting.
Confirm a human has approved any scale or restart, and that restarting won't drop in-flight traffic beyond what is acceptable (traces show no errors currently, E2).
Identify the last deployed version so a rollback target is known.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale the deployment back to its original replica count (`kubectl scale`), and if a restart or deploy rollback was performed, use `kubectl rollout undo deployment/recommendationservice` to return to the previous revision.
